backlog.spec: Add RDKit's EState fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.EStateFingerprinter.FingerprintMol, the count-based 79-dim vector) and the per-molecule sum and max of EState indices (rdkit.Chem.EState.EState.EStateIndices) as extra columns. Concatenate them to the existing descriptor block so the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost members see them. Leave the Ridge input and all hyperparameters unchanged. Guard each call with try/except and fall back to zeros so that failed molecules do not crash the fit.
backlog.title: EState fingerprint and EState atom indices

backlog.spec: All three tree members and the Ridge are fit once with a single random_state=seed. Because the dataset is small (970 molecules) and the folds test unseen scaffolds, a noticeable part of each member's prediction is fitting noise that averaging over seeds removes for free. Modify fit_predict so that, for each of the three tree models, the model is fit three times with random_state = seed, seed+1, seed+2 (or random_seed for CatBoost), each prediction vector is converted to normalized ranks with rankdata(p)/len(p), and the three rank vectors are averaged into that member's single prediction before the member-level mean is taken. The Ridge is deterministic and needs no change. Reduce n_estimators/iterations by a factor of about two (RF 150, LightGBM 250, CatBoost 250) so the job still fits comfortably inside the 10-minute, 15-fit budget; the seed average should more than compensate for the smaller individual models. Keep the 0.7/0.3 final blend untouched.
backlog.title: Seed-average every ensemble member over three seeds

backlog.spec: Append rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR2D (192 values) and the BCUT2D descriptors (Descriptors.BCUT2D_* are already in descList, so use only AUTOCORR2D) to the descriptor matrix. Clean them with nan_to_num and clip. Place them before the ErG block so that the shapes of the last N_BITS columns stay valid for Ridge.
backlog.title: Extra descriptor blocks: BCUT and autocorrelation

backlog.spec: After computing the 3 rank-normalized tree member predictions and the Ridge rank, compute the consensus c as the mean of all 4. Replace each tree member p with 0.7*p+0.3*c before the final blend. Then make the final blend as before. This is a light regularization of the ensemble.
backlog.title: Shrink members toward consensus

backlog.spec: Replace the LGBMRegressor member with LGBMRegressor(objective='huber', alpha=0.3) on the rank target y in [0,1]. Keep the other hyperparameters. This makes the loss robust to outliers in the rank target, so it can differ from the squared-error members.
backlog.title: Lambdarank-style LightGBM member swap

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py at all and simply run the current file again as a replicate job. The incumbent (RDKit descriptors + 315-dim ErG + Morgan counts feeding the RF/LightGBM/CatBoost rank average at 0.7 blended with a 0.3 Ridge on log1p Morgan counts) scored 0.4745 on a single run, a 0.0186 gain over the previous accepted state, which is only about 2.7 noise sd and has never been confirmed. A second independent run gives the mean_adjusted estimate two observations and tells us whether the ErG block is a real improvement or a lucky draw; everything downstream (blend-weight tuning, new members) is being judged against this number, so it is worth one slot to pin it down. Do not touch any setting, seed handling, or ordering, so the only difference between the two runs is the harness fold assignment noise.
backlog.title: Replicate the ErG incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Give the tree members (RF, LightGBM, CatBoost) only the descriptor and ErG columns, dropping the 2048 Morgan count columns from their input matrix. Keep the Morgan count block only for the Ridge member, which already uses the last N_BITS columns of the feature matrix. This leaves the fingerprint information to the linear model and gives the trees a smaller, denser feature set. Compute the column slice once and reuse it for train and test. Everything else in the blend is unchanged.
backlog.title: Route Morgan counts away from tree members

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before any model is trained, score every column of the training matrix Xtr by the absolute Spearman correlation between the column and the rank target y, computed on the training fold only. Keep the top 400 columns by this score, and apply the same column mask to Xte. Use the reduced matrix for the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost members. Leave the Ridge input on the full Morgan count block. Ties and constant columns get score 0. This is a supervised, fold-internal filter and must not look at test molecules.
backlog.title: Within-fold Spearman feature filter

backlog.spec: The outer blend currently mixes tree models with one linear model on fingerprint counts; no member exploits smooth nonlinear structure in the continuous physicochemical descriptors. Inside fit_predict, build a descriptor-only matrix from the first columns of Xtr/Xte that correspond to the RDKit descriptors plus the ErG block (i.e. everything except the last N_BITS columns), fit a sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(200, n_train), random_state=seed) on the training rows and apply it to both, then fit KernelRidge(alpha=1.0, kernel='rbf', gamma=1.0/n_features) on the rank target. Rank-normalize its prediction and make the final output 0.6 * tree_mean + 0.25 * ridge_morgan_rank + 0.15 * rbf_rank, keeping the existing tree average and Morgan Ridge exactly as they are. This differs from the rejected averaged-kernel experiment, which mixed an RBF descriptor kernel into a single kernel ridge; here it is a separate, independently rank-normalized blend member, which is the pattern that has actually produced the gains in this run.
backlog.title: Add an RBF kernel ridge member on normalized descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member's hyperparameters with boosting_type='dart', drop_rate 0.1, skip_drop 0.5, n_estimators 400, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, extra_trees=True, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.8 and subsample_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, with random_state set to seed. Keep the other members and the blend exactly as they are. The change only affects the boosting scheme of one member, so any gain or loss can be attributed to it.
backlog.title: LightGBM dart boosting with extra trees

backlog.spec: Add a member: sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers (256,64), alpha 1e-2, early_stopping, max_iter 300, random_state=seed) trained on QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') applied to the descriptor+ErG columns, which are the first Xtr.shape[1]-N_BITS columns. Average 3 seeds. Blend it by rank at 15% and scale the other weights by 0.85.
backlog.title: Random-projection MLP on descriptors+ErG

backlog.spec: The loss is Spearman correlation, so a member trained directly on pairwise ordering rather than squared error is a principled source of diversity. Add an LGBMRanker member inside fit_predict: discretize the rank target into 32 integer relevance levels with np.floor(y * 32).astype(int) clipped to [0, 31], treat the whole training set as one query group (group=[len(y)]), and fit LGBMRanker(objective='lambdarank', n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_samples=10, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) on the same full Xtr used by the other tree members. Its raw scores are only meaningful up to a monotone transform, which is exactly what the existing pipeline needs: rank-normalize with rankdata(p)/len(p) and add it as a fourth element of the preds list so it enters the 0.7-weighted tree average, leaving the 0.3 Ridge term untouched. If LGBMRanker's single-group setup errors out, fall back to LGBMRegressor with objective='huber' and report that in the log rather than crashing.
backlog.title: Add a pairwise-rank LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Run the current train.py exactly as it is, with no edits at all, to obtain a second independent measurement of the incumbent. The ErG gain (0.4745, a 0.0186 improvement) rests on a single run, and several later slots have measured 0.4736-0.4787 around it, so the true level of the incumbent is uncertain by roughly one noise sd. Submit the file byte-identical (an empty edit set) and report the official loss; this run anchors every subsequent delta and tells us whether the recent string of flat results reflects a plateau or a lucky incumbent reading. No code, feature, or hyperparameter change of any kind.
backlog.title: Replicate the ErG incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Build a new member in which a standardized Ridge (alpha 10) is first fit on the standardized descriptor+ErG columns only, using training data to fit. Compute its in-sample residuals on the training set, then fit a RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, max_features 0.2, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on Xtr to predict those residuals. The member prediction is the Ridge prediction plus the RF residual prediction on test molecules. Rank-normalize it and include it as an extra member in the existing rank average, with the Ridge member and blend weights unchanged. Use the seed argument for all randomness.
backlog.title: Ridge-then-RF residual stacking member

backlog.spec: Add a small block of counts computed with RDKit SMARTS patterns on each molecule: carboxylic acids ([CX3](=O)[OX2H1,OX1-]), tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, phenols, aliphatic amines (primary, secondary, tertiary, not amides or anilines), amidines/guanidines, quaternary N, and a zwitterion flag (acid and base both present). Also add a crude pH 7.4 logD proxy = Crippen MolLogP minus 3 if an acid is present minus 1 if a base is present. Append these columns to the descriptor block before the Morgan counts. Keep all other members unchanged so the effect of ionization information is isolated.
backlog.title: Ionization-state SMARTS counts as extra features

backlog.spec: Wrap the existing modelling code in a loop over three derived seeds (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000) and average the final blended rank predictions across them. Refactor fit_predict so the features are computed once (they do not depend on the seed), then for each derived seed build the RF, LightGBM, and CatBoost members with that seed, form the current 0.7 tree-average plus 0.3 Ridge blend, rank-normalize the result, and finally return the mean of the three rank-normalized blends. The Ridge member is deterministic, so it can be fitted once outside the loop and reused. This reduces the variance that each member's random column and row sampling injects into the fold predictions; since the metric is Spearman on only about 190 test molecules per fold, seed variance is a real part of the measured loss. Check the runtime budget: if three passes exceed roughly seven minutes, drop the CatBoost iterations to 300 rather than reducing the number of seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-bag the whole pipeline over three seeds

backlog.spec: Add a fourth outer blend member using sklearn.cross_decomposition.PLSRegression, which is well suited to the wide, highly collinear RDKit descriptor block and gives a different inductive bias from both the trees and the sparse-count Ridge. Take the non-fingerprint columns of Xtr/Xte (RDKit descriptors plus the 315 ErG features), standardize them with StandardScaler fitted on the training rows, clip to [-5, 5] to tame descriptor outliers, and fit PLSRegression(n_components=12, scale=False) on the rank target. Flatten its prediction, rank-normalize with rankdata(p)/len(p), and change the final blend to 0.6 * tree_mean + 0.25 * ridge_rank + 0.15 * pls_rank with the rest of fit_predict unchanged. PLS is fast (a few seconds for 970 rows) and the component count is the only knob, so a follow-up could test 6 or 20 components if this direction shows promise.
backlog.title: Add a PLS regression member on descriptors and ErG

backlog.spec: Add a new feature block from the Avalon fingerprinter, which encodes substructures with a different hashing scheme from Morgan and has not yet been tried (atom-pair and torsion counts were, and were flat). Write def avalon(smiles) that uses from rdkit.Avalon import pyAvalonTools and returns np.array of pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(mol, nBits=1024).ToList() per molecule as float32. In fit_predict, insert this block into both Xtr and Xte between the ErG block and the Morgan counts, i.e. np.hstack([descriptors(s), erg(s), avalon(s), featurize(s)]). Leave the Ridge member reading the last N_BITS columns, so it still sees only the Morgan counts and the change is isolated to the three tree models, whose column subsampling (max_features 0.2, colsample 0.3, rsm 0.2) can exploit the extra substructure views. Runtime cost is small; if Avalon is unavailable in the environment, fall back cleanly by catching ImportError and returning a zero-width array.
backlog.title: Add an Avalon fingerprint count block

backlog.spec: Change the CatBoost member to depth 8, iterations 1000, learning_rate 0.03, l2_leaf_reg 10, rsm 0.2, random_seed seed and thread_count 8, keeping the same descriptor+ErG+Morgan input matrix. Deeper symmetric trees with stronger L2 regularization may capture interactions the depth-6 model misses while staying stable on small data. Leave the other members and the blend weights unchanged so the change is isolated to this model.
backlog.title: Deeper, more regularized CatBoost member

backlog.spec: Add one new member to the blend: sklearn.cross_decomposition.PLSRegression with n_components=10 fitted on the standardized descriptor-plus-ErG columns (i.e. the feature matrix excluding the last N_BITS Morgan columns), predicting the rank target. Standardize with StandardScaler fitted on train and applied to test, ravel the PLS output, rank-normalize the prediction the same way the other members are, and blend it in at 15% while scaling the existing combination to 85% (keep the internal 0.7 tree-average / 0.3 Ridge split inside that 85%). PLS finds supervised low-rank directions in correlated continuous descriptors, a very different inductive bias from both the trees and the unregularized-direction Ridge on sparse counts, and the descriptor and ErG blocks are exactly the dense correlated kind of input PLS handles well.
backlog.title: Add a PLS regression member on descriptors and ErG

memo:
Helped: target handling and, above all, ensembling diverse members. The rank target gave 0.5286/0.5252 (replicated). The rank-averaged RF+LightGBM+kernel ensemble reached 0.5083. A 30% Ridge member on log1p Morgan counts gave 0.4922/0.4939 (replicated). ErG pharmacophore features gave the incumbent, 0.4745 (1 run only, a 0.0186 gain, about 2.7 noise sd).
Did not help: single tree models (ExtraTrees 0.6287/0.5571, RF 0.5564, LightGBM 0.5442), SVR 0.5699, MLP 0.5515, scaffold weights 0.5477, Gaussian quantile target 0.5289. Recent additions were flat or worse: CatBoost 0.4745, kernel ridge member 0.4787, atom-pair counts 0.4777, kNN 0.4812, NNLS blend 0.4782, torsion counts 0.4739, RF tweaks 0.4768/0.4743. All of these are within noise (sd 0.0070).
Next: replicate ErG first. Then tune the Ridge blend weight and alpha, and try other feature blocks such as MACCS. Read train.py before writing specs, since several slots were lost to aborts.
